walkthroughs.body_html:
Programming Concepts — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Programming Concepts brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Programming Concepts.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which is a high-level programming language?
options: Assembly
Machine code
Python
Binary
Internet Data Engine
Integrated Development Environment
Internal Debugging Editor
Interpreted Dynamic Executable

mcqs.q: Which item is removed first from a stack?
options: The most recently added (top) - LIFO.
Any item, randomly.
The first one added (FIFO).
To make the function run faster.

mcqs.q: Why must a recursive function have a base case?
options: To make the function run faster.
Because the syntax requires it.
Copy code from any unrelated class.
Without it, the function calls itself indefinitely, causing a stack overflow.

mcqs.q: What does inheritance allow a subclass to do?
options: To make the function run faster.
Reuse and extend the attributes and methods of its superclass.
Replace the superclass entirely.
Copy code from any unrelated class.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “IDE”?
options: Non-executing text in source code that explains the program to human readers.
Set of rules defining valid combinations of symbols and keywords in a programming language.
Meaning of a syntactically valid program - what the code actually does when executed.
Integrated Development Environment: editor, compiler/interpreter, debugger and tools combined in one application.

Assembly or machine code, closer to hardware, providing direct control of the processor.
